# 3.6 Interval DP

Phase 3 (Recursion to dynamic programming), target rating 1500–1900. Bank status: not started.

## Patterns

### Split point of a segment (`merge-split`)

dp[l][r] is the best over a split point k of combining [l, k] and [k+1, r] (merging stones, cutting a stick, matrix order).

**Works because:** An optimal solution on [l, r] consists of independent optimal solutions on two sub-segments.

### Taking from either end (`take-from-ends`)

Players or a process remove items only from the ends, so the remaining items always form one contiguous segment.

**Works because:** The state is fully described by the remaining segment [l, r].

### Palindromes inside segments (`palindrome-segment`)

Longest palindromic subsequence, or fewest insertions to make a palindrome, from [l+1, r−1], [l+1, r], and [l, r−1].

**Works because:** The answer for [l, r] depends only on its first and last characters and the inner segments.

### First element pairs with some k (`first-element-match`)

The first element of the segment is removed together with some element k, splitting the rest into independent parts (removing equal blocks, bracket pairs).

**Works because:** After choosing the partner k of l, the parts inside and outside of (l, k) do not interact.
